name: Cookie Store API
plain: Reads and changes cookies asynchronously and gets change events, including in service workers.
meaning: A site can watch and edit its own cookies without parsing document.cookie. It sees only non-HttpOnly cookies for its own origin.

web.api: cookieStore.get(), getAll(), set(), delete(); cookiechange event

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
steps: cookiechange event fires in other tabs and service workers

limits.headline: Can watch and change the site's own cookies, but not hidden ones or other sites' cookies
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the site's script checks or sets a cookie
can: List and change the site's own cookies that scripts may see
Get a notice when its own cookies change, including in a background script
Keep your sign in in step across tabs
cannot: Work from outside the site's own address
Be sure to stop cookie syncing, which you stop by clearing cookies or blocking trackers

story.what_it_is: A page can read and change cookies the modern way and hear about changes, even in background scripts.

marketing.name: Cookie Store API
marketing.pitch: Offers an async way to read and write cookies and to listen for changes, including in service workers.

story.for_you: You never see it. Sites use it to remember your login and settings. If you clear cookies, the site will see the change.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to manage login, consent choices and tracking IDs without blocking the page. Change events let them react when cookies are added or cleared. It works inside background scripts too.

use_cases.example: A store keeps your cart and login in cookies, and notices if they are cleared to rebuild your session.
An ad script watches for cookie changes and re-creates its ID if you clear it.
An analytics tool reads and writes its visitor ID cookie, and sends a new event when it changes.
A browser game portal stores your sign in and settings in cookies, and syncs across tabs.
A bank page detects when its session cookie is removed and logs out the tab.
A news site stores your cookie consent choices and reads them in the background scripts.
A streaming site shares a login across tabs using cookie change events.

technical_bounds: HTTPS only; cannot read HttpOnly cookies
Cookie size limit 4096 bytes for name plus value; about 180 cookies per domain in Chrome, 50 per domain in Firefox (older), 150 in Safari
Max Expires/Max-Age cap is 400 days in Chrome (Chrome 104)
Third-party contexts follow normal third-party cookie blocking and the Storage Access API
Support per MDN BCD: Chrome and Edge 87, Safari 18.4, Firefox 140

history.change: Cookie Max-Age and Expires capped at 400 days
Cookie Store API ships in Safari
Cookie Store API ships in Firefox
